label: sparse: original-phase token after "a d" bigram (+ scattered early copy steps)
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (0.009% of steps), never at t<2 or the delimiter. About 2/3 of mass is in the original phase, strongly enriched for steps right after a d (prev_tok d, 15.6x), especially after an a-d bigram (prev2 a, 11.9x), with in_tok among g/h/f/k/z/c. The other third is in the early copy phase (recall_idx 1-3) with in_tok g/z/h, mostly in sequences starting with g/z/o. Every token-context predicate tried has very low precision: prev_tok==d covers 44% of activations at 0.3% precision, and the best narrow clause (a-d-X) gets F1 0.16. Activation seems to depend on longer specific histories that these variables do not capture. Magnitude varies little (median 0.116, max 0.186) and was not tied to any variable.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=g (+4.83), phase=2 & in_tok=z (+3.99), prev_tok=d (+3.84), phase=2 & out_tok=z (+3.61), prev2_tok=a (+3.27), phase=2 & out_tok=o (+2.85). Lower it: correct=1 (-4.81), orig_idx=-1 (-3.32), prev_tok=g (-2.25), in_first=0 (-1.25).
